run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T15:53:22Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is a downstream symptom of ProductCatalogService calls stalling. At 15:53:22Z frontend-proxy ingress error spans jumped from 0 to ~151 per 5m and then plateaued at ~360-607 per 5m. The proxy logs show `504 UT response_timeout` at its 15000 ms upstream timeout for exactly the routes that need product-catalog (GET /api/products/{id}, GET /api/recommendations, POST /api/checkout), while /api/cart, /api/data and GET / returned 200 in 1-249 ms, and traces show frontend /api/products/[productId] returning HTTP 500 on `14 UNAVAILABLE: read ECONNRESET`. The reset terminates at product-catalog's ClusterIP 100.64.188.136:8080, and product-catalog's own GetProduct handler spans are only 105-122 microseconds while client spans for the same calls last 20.0006 s or 5.99-28.21 s (error 14), so the fault is on the product-catalog side of the wire, not in the frontend handler. product-catalog's completed-span rate and CPU usage both collapsed from ~15:53 onward while its pod stayed Running/Ready with 0 restarts and flat memory, which rules out crash/OOM/CPU-throttling and leaves the pod's response path (a fixed ~20 s delay and connection resets) as the origin. The exact mechanism (network delay/loss injection versus another fault on that pod) is not verifiable in this Run because change/fault-injection history is not integrated, so the deepest confirmed causal step stops at the product-catalog pod.

claims.text: frontend-proxy ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate was 0 up to 15:52:22Z, jumped to 151.11 per 5m at 15:53:22Z (the alert start) and stayed at 288.9-607.1 per 5m through 16:05:22Z; 'router frontend egress' error spans appeared from 15:57:22Z (11.1-15.2 per 5m).
Over the 15 minutes ending 16:08:37Z frontend-proxy recorded 1113.26 ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, 881.98 ingress STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans and 22.08 'router frontend egress' error spans.

frontend-proxy ingress spans sampled in 15:55-16:05Z contain 9 spans with http.status_code 504 and 1 with http.status_code 500, each lasting about 15.00 s, with the paired 'router frontend egress' span carrying error="true"/http.status_code="0"; the load-generator GET/POST spans in the same traces record 504/500.

frontend-proxy logs between 15:59:21Z and 15:59:42Z record `504 UT response_timeout` with a 15000 ms upstream response time for "GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO", "GET /api/recommendations?productIds=LS4PSXUNUM" and "POST /api/checkout", while "POST /api/cart", "GET /api/data?contextKeys=..." and "GET /" returned 200 in 1-249 ms against the same upstream `frontend`.

In the frontend, spans "executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId]" and "GET /api/products/{productId}" returned HTTP 500 after 11.09-28.21 s with `14 UNAVAILABLE: read ECONNRESET`, and their child spans `grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct` lasted 5.99-22.79 s with rpc.grpc.status_code 14; several of these errors on different traces all ended at the same instant 15:55:47.658Z.

For the same ProductCatalogService/GetProduct call the product-catalog server span completed in 105 microseconds with rpc.grpc.status_code 0, while the frontend client span lasted 26.796 s and failed with `14 UNAVAILABLE: read ECONNRESET` - the server side was fast, the response never reached the caller in time.

checkout's client spans to oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct during 15:55-15:57Z measured 20.000612 s, 20.000625 s, 20.000679 s and 20.000719 s (rpc.grpc.status_code 0) plus one 65.877 s span, while the matching product-catalog server spans were 106-122 microseconds; the durations cluster at a fixed ~20 s on the response path.

checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder span failed with otel.status_code ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code 13 and message `failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"0PUK6V6EV0"`, and its child checkout span oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct failed with rpc.grpc.status_code 14 and `error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer`.
The endpoint the reset came from, 100.64.188.136:8080, is the otel-demo Service `product-catalog` (ClusterIP 100.64.188.136, port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog).

product-catalog's completed-span rate collapsed: 2-minute increases were 860-957 spans through 15:51:22Z, 156 at 15:53:22Z, 6.67 at 15:55:22Z, 21.33 at 15:57:22Z and 0 from 15:59:22Z onward, and both its span names (oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts) read 0 per minute thereafter.

product-catalog's container CPU usage fell from ~0.0106-0.0151 cores before 15:53:22Z to 0.0009-0.0025 cores afterwards, and its CFS throttling ratio fell from ~0.15-0.20 to 0.02-0.09; its memory working set stayed flat at ~11.8-13.8 MB against a 30Mi limit (frontend working set rose 126 MB -> 173 MB against a 200Mi limit).

The product-catalog pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 is Running and Ready (Ready condition since 15:15:34Z) with restartCount 0, empty lastState, no liveness/readiness/startup probes and a 15m CPU / 30Mi memory limit; frontend-675fd7b5c5-64blr and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-xh66d are likewise Running/Ready with restartCount 0.

Total span volume fell between 15:45:22Z and 16:05:22Z (10-minute increases): frontend 28541 -> 3797, frontend-proxy 13184 -> 3158, cart 10197 -> 2063, checkout 4956 -> 420, product-catalog 6715 -> 18.8, recommendation 1526 -> 1.1, ad 1172 -> 288.

In the 10 minutes to 16:05:22Z the frontend issued 0 completed calls to ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and 0 to RecommendationService/ListRecommendations, while AdService/GetAds (133.99, 0 errors), CartService/GetCart (385.35) and CartService/AddItem (249.15) continued normally - only the product-catalog-dependent paths stopped completing.

product-catalog's container kept logging "Product Found" / "Reloading Product Catalog..." / "Loaded 10 products" up to 15:58:35Z: the read for 15:50:00-16:08:37Z returned 1066 lines, the newest 40 of which span 15:57:04Z to 15:58:35Z.

In the 10 minutes to 16:05:22Z the only services with error spans were frontend-proxy (ingress 880.32, router frontend egress 23.25), frontend (GET 23.25, POST 11.04, POST /api/checkout 107.04, executing api route /api/checkout 107.41, grpc CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 58.69) and recommendation (/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 1.11); ad, cart, currency, email, accounting, payment, shipping, quote, image-provider, kafka, fraud-detection and product-catalog had no error-span increase on that metric.

All 21 otel-demo pods were Running; the only container with restarts was fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-n7vmf (restartCount 2), whose container was Created and Started at 15:47:37Z, before the alert start; the other events returned for the window are repeated Normal "Updated" events on product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9, and no OOMKilled/Evicted/Unhealthy events were returned.

All 19 Services in otel-demo resolve to pod selectors, including frontend (100.71.161.142:8080), frontend-proxy (100.71.231.114:8080) and product-catalog (100.64.188.136:8080), so the failing calls had a valid service endpoint to reach.

The firing alert is a symptom of ProductCatalogService calls stalling: every frontend-proxy route that timed out or 500'd (GET /api/products/{id}, GET /api/recommendations, POST /api/checkout) depends on product-catalog, and the corresponding client spans to product-catalog fail with 'read ECONNRESET' / 20 s waits while all non-product-catalog routes on the same frontend stayed fast.

The fault sits on the product-catalog pod's response path rather than in its application logic: handler spans complete in 105-122 microseconds, but clients on two different callers (frontend on node i-05386ef47c25d9530 and checkout on node i-0b2137ceca968ac10) see fixed ~20.0006 s completions or ECONNRESET from 100.64.188.136:8080, which is consistent with an injected response delay / connection reset applied to that pod's traffic; the exact fault mechanism cannot be confirmed because no network telemetry and no change history are available.

Frontend resource saturation as the cause is rejected: in the same traces where GetProduct hung, frontend CartService/AddItem and GetCart spans completed in 1.8-2.0 ms and 1.1-1.3 ms, /api/cart and /api/data returned 200 in 1-249 ms through the same proxy, and the frontend's CFS throttling ratio fell from ~0.19-0.26 to ~0.06-0.16 during the incident instead of rising.

product-catalog crash, OOM or CPU throttling as the cause is rejected: restartCount is 0 with empty lastState and Ready=True, memory working set stayed ~11.8-13.8 MB (limit 30Mi), CPU usage and CFS throttling both fell after 15:53:22Z, and no OOMKilled/Evicted events were returned.

The fraud-detection container restarted twice (Created/Started 15:47:37Z, before the 15:53:22Z alert) and its only error spans are ~1.1 per 5m /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream errors that also appear for ad and recommendation before and during the incident; no error-rate or latency evidence ties it to the frontend-proxy error surge, so it is a change in the window for another reason, not part of this impact.

Look for a network-level fault or configuration change applied to the product-catalog pod/service around 15:53:22Z (e.g. delay/loss/connection-reset injection, tc/netem rules, or an endpoint change), and compare its kernel/network counters (retransmits, drops) and pod network stats; the fixed 20.0006 s client completions with microsecond server spans are the signature to match.

Once the product-catalog response path is restored, re-check frontend /api/products/[productId], /api/recommendations and /api/checkout latencies and the frontend-proxy ingress error ratio, and consider whether the proxy's 15 s upstream timeout is appropriate for these routes.

gaps: Change/fault-injection history is not integrated (data_sources.not_integrated = change_history), so I could not verify whether a delay/partition/reset experiment or a configuration change was applied to product-catalog at 15:53:22Z - the mechanism behind the ~20 s responses and ECONNRESET remains a hypothesis.

No network-level telemetry (TCP retransmits, packet loss, conntrack, per-pod network stats) is available, so the direction and type of the network fault on the product-catalog path could not be measured directly.
The NetworkPolicy query for namespace otel-demo returned no_data, so whether a NetworkPolicy restricts product-catalog traffic is unverified - the absence of a policy is not established.

The keyword-filtered read of product-catalog logs (err|error|fatal|panic|fail|reset|timeout over 15:30-16:08:37Z) returned no_data rather than a matching set, so it neither confirms nor excludes error lines in that container's output.

The alerting rule named RequestErrorRate returned no data from list_prometheus_rules, so its exact expression, threshold and the meaning of the reported value 1.422222222222222 could not be verified; that value is only what the alert payload states.
The frontend container's log reads returned no_data / zero lines for both queried windows and it has no previous instance, so frontend application logs could not be used to corroborate its errors.

rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and kube_pod_container/kube_pod_status series returned no data for the queried selectors, so gRPC/HTTP latency and error ratios and Kubernetes-level container status metrics could not be cross-checked from those series.

product-catalog's log stream returned no lines after 15:58:35Z, but log absence cannot prove that its process stopped serving; whether it froze or kept handling some requests after that time is unknown.
A CRD query for chaos/fault-injection custom resources exceeded the result size limit and returned an error, so the presence of fault-injection objects could not be checked.
Kubernetes objects are the current state at query time and events only cover their own in-window timestamps, so the earlier state of the involved objects cannot be proven from them.

recommendation's span volume collapsed (1526 -> 1.1 per 10m) but I did not observe recommendation's own failure evidence tied to this cause, so whether it is independently affected is unestablished; its only error signal is the shared ~1.1 per 5m flagd EventStream error seen for ad and recommendation alike.
A separate product-catalog span search returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE and was only partially read (40 of 224 rows), so the sampled trace view of product-catalog is not exhaustive.
next_steps: Retrieve change/fault-injection history for namespace otel-demo around 2026-11-16T15:53:22Z, specifically anything targeting pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 or the product-catalog Service, to confirm or refute an injected delay/reset.
Inspect node i-0b2137ceca968ac10 and its kube-proxy/conntrack and the product-catalog pod's network interface counters for retransmissions, drops and resets in the 15:50-16:05 window.
Pull the alerting rule definition for RequestErrorRate from the Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration that owns it, since the in-cluster rule set did not return it.

Compare product-catalog client latency from a second independent caller (e.g. a direct gRPC probe to product-catalog:8080) before and after the restore to validate that the ~20 s response delay is gone.
List NetworkPolicies in otel-demo again, and if any exist, review their selectors against the product-catalog pods to rule out policy-driven blocking.
